subject: Clarify end-of-term notice & termination-for-convenience language

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft MSA redline: term / auto-renew / termination for convenience

Sam —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Attached is a clean redline of the MSA + order form with the sections we discussed highlighted (term, auto-renew mechanics, and termination-for-convenience). A few items we'd like to resolve before legal does a full pass:

- Auto-renew: Redwood typically sets 12-month renewal terms with a 60-day notice to opt out. Can you confirm if Acme requires 90 days?
- Termination for convenience: we can offer a mutual convenience right, but Redwood asks for either (a) pro-rated payment for committed capacity through 60 days or (b) a 60-day notice paired with payment of the remainder of the committed billing period. Which approach is acceptable to you?
- Notice windows: please confirm whether Acme procurement needs written notice to be provided to a particular mailbox (procurement@acme.com) and any internal escalation contacts.

Next steps I suggest: if you can confirm preference on notice window & the termination-for-convenience economic approach, we can prepare a counter-redline for legal to consider. I'm looping Karthik and Ben for commercial input.

Attachments: ACME_MSA_redline_steph_20260718.docx (redline), TermSummary.txt (one-pager summary)

Best,

Stephanie Nguyen

From: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@acme.com>

Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft MSA redline: term / auto-renew / termination for convenience

Stephanie —

Appreciate the redline and the clear summary. A few quick answers from procurement/legal side: 

1) Auto-renew: Acme policy prefers a 12-month renewal but requires a 90-day opt-out window for any contract with an enterprise spend commitment. That said, procurement is willing to accept a 60-day window if we can add a firm notification path (procurement@acme.com with a read receipt to legal@acme.com).

2) Termination for convenience: Legal would like a mutual right but wants a clear economic boundary. Our initial ask is termination with 90 days' notice and pro-rated credits for unused service days beyond that 90-day period. We understand Redwood's position on committed capacity — if Redwood insists on committed-payment protection, legal asks that it be capped to a maximum of 90 days of committed fees.

I've attached our preliminary comments (ACME_comments_legal_20260719.docx). Legal will do a formal redline after internal clearance; procurement flagged that they need to see final language before routing to our CFO.

Two asks from us: please confirm (a) the mailbox to send formal termination notices to, and (b) whether Redwood can agree to cap termination repayment to 90 days of committed fees.

Thanks — Sam
Sam Jenkins
Director, Strategic Procurement | Acme Corp

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft MSA redline: term / auto-renew / termination for convenience

Team —

Reading Sam's note and Acme's comments. Commercial proposal we should consider before legal tradeoffs: 

Option A (compromise): 12-month term auto-renews; customer can opt out with 60 days written notice. Termination for convenience allowed by either party with 60 days' notice; customer pays pro-rated committed fees capped at 90 days. This preserves Redwood's ability to protect reserved capacity while giving Acme predictability.

Option B (more favorable to Redwood): 12-month term auto-renews with 60-day notice; termination for convenience allowed with 60 days' notice but Redwood is entitled to the lesser of (i) pro-rated committed fees for the remainder of the contract term, or (ii) 90 days' committed fees.

If legal prefers a clean cap, Option A is easiest to explain to procurement/CFO. Laura — can you draft tidy MSA language for Option A that we can send to Acme legal for review? I'll be ready to present rationale to our finance lead if they push back.

Ben — please flag any margin/forecasting implications if we accept the 90-day cap.

Karthik
Head of Sales Operations | Redwood Inference

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed MSA language — termination & notice windows

Sam / team —

Thanks for the quick response and the attached comments. Per Karthik's ask, I've drafted proposed MSA text for Option A (compromise) for you to review. Please note this is a commercial-legal compromise designed to address Acme's notice concerns while protecting Redwood's committed capacity economics.

Proposed redline (new Section 9.2 — Termination for Convenience):

"Either party may terminate this Agreement for convenience by providing at least sixty (60) days' prior written notice to the other party. In the event Customer terminates for convenience, Customer shall be responsible for payment of any unpaid portion of committed fees, which shall be capped at an amount equal to ninety (90) days of Customer's committed monthly fees as of the date of notice. Such payment shall be due within thirty (30) days of the effective date of termination. Termination notices must be sent to procurement@acme.com with a copy to legal@acme.com."

Auto-renew language (Section 3.1 — Term and Renewal):

"The Initial Term of the Order Form shall be twelve (12) months. The Order Form will automatically renew for successive twelve (12) month periods unless either party delivers written notice of non-renewal at least sixty (60) days prior to the end of the then-current Term. Notices of non-renewal by Customer must be sent to procurement@acme.com and legal@acme.com."

If that aligns with Acme's position, we can incorporate these redlines into the MSA and send a tracked change copy for Acme legal to accept or further amend. 

Attachments: redline_legal_suggestion_20260721.docx

Would you like us to schedule a 30-minute legal-to-legal call to finalize quickly?

Regards,

Laura Bennett
